title: Iran-Contra: Tower Commission & Walsh Report
summary: The Reagan administration secretly sold arms to Iran and diverted proceeds to Nicaragua's Contras despite the Boland Amendment ban. Tower Commission (Feb 1987): Reagan's 'lax managerial style.' Walsh final report (Aug 1993): 14 officials charged, 11 convictions/guilty pleas; arms sales 'contravened U.S. Government policy'; systematic document destruction documented. George H.W. Bush's Dec 24, 1992 pardons ended the probe.

sources.label: Tower Commission Report — full text (Internet Archive, U.S. government-documents mirror)

tldr: The Tower Commission (Feb 26, 1987) found the NSC ran covert arms sales to Iran — whose excess profits were very likely diverted to the Contras — while President Reagan's hands-off management style meant he never forced the operation through real review or accountability.
ai_summary:
AI review of the President's Special Review Board ('Tower Commission') report — cover letter dated February 26, 1987, signed by Chairman John Tower, Edmund Muskie and Brent Scowcroft — read in full (OCR text, 182k words; conclusion sections read verbatim):
- Timeline documented: first TOW-missile shipment to Iran via Israel (Aug–Sep 1985), HAWK missiles (Nov 1985), then four direct U.S.-managed deliveries in 1986 including 'Operation Recovery' — 1,000 TOW missiles.
- Diversion evidence: Israel charged Iran ~$3M over cost on the 1985 TOWs (disposition unknown); the four 1986 U.S. deliveries charged ~$20M over cost ($6.3M Feb TOWs, $8.5M May/Aug HAWK parts, $5M Oct TOWs), most of it unaccounted for in Swiss accounts under Richard Secord's control. 'There was considerable evidence before the Board of a diversion to support the Contras. But the Board had no hard proof.' Attorney General Meese told the Board that both Poindexter and North told him a diversion had occurred.
- On Reagan: 'The President did not seem to be aware of the way in which the operation was implemented.' His 'management style is to put the principal responsibility for policy review and implementation on the shoulders of his advisors'; 'At no time did he insist upon accountability and performance review.' 'The NSC process did not fail, it simply was largely ignored.'
- Note on record-summary accuracy: the summary's Tower characterization is accurate, but its Walsh final-report details (14 officials charged, 11 convictions, Aug 1993) and the Dec 24, 1992 Bush pardons are not in this 1987 document — they postdate it. Flagging for the record author.
